_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description:
A rotated JPEG is commented on in the pixels that were rendered: the conversation read {{IMAGE}}, a 100x50 JPEG tagged to be rotated 90° for display, with read_image. "The overlay" is ".image-comment-overlay"; "the frame" is ".image-comment-overlay .image-comment-frame" (it shrink-wraps the image, so its box is the image's displayed pixels and a fraction of it is a fraction of the image). "Drag from (a, b) to (c, d)" means: move the mouse over the frame at offsets (a × its width, b × its height) from its top-left, press the left button, move to (c × width, d × height) in N steps (5 unless said otherwise), and release; read the frame's box with getBoundingClientRect when computing the offsets. "Drag the middle half" is a drag from (0.25, 0.25) to (0.75, 0.75). The open comment dialog has its title ".diff-viewer-comment-dialog-handle" (it names the region being commented on), its input ".diff-viewer-comment-input" and its button "Add Comment" (name exactly that). window.geometry() returns the WxH+X+Y region the dialog title names; window.middleHalf(W, H) returns "ok" if that region is the middle half of a WxH image, within tolerance, and otherwise what is off; window.keepGeometry() keeps the current geometry for later, and window.kept(i) returns the i-th one kept (from 0). Check the message input's (data-testid "message-input") value with an eval comparing it to the exact string, building it with window.kept(i) where it says G or Gi; \n is a newline. Perform the steps in order.
1. Navigate to /c/image. Wait (up to 30s) for the first ".screenshot-tool .commentable-image" (the image) to be visible. 
2. The premise: the browser really does rotate it. Without this the test would pass on a build that never had the bug to fix. The image's naturalWidth should come (within 15s) to be exactly 50, and its naturalHeight should then be exactly 100.
3. Click the image. The overlay's ".image-comment-hint" should contain "Drag a box".
4. Drag the middle half. The middle half of the image as displayed, in the displayed image's own 50x100 space -- not 100x50, which would describe a different region: window.middleHalf(50, 100) should return exactly "ok". Keep the geometry (G0).
5. Fill the dialog's input with "rotated" and click "Add Comment". The message input's value should be exactly "> image {{IMAGE}} [region G0 of 50x100, auto-orient first]\nrotated\n\n".
